source: Essex CC Annual Plan and Budget 2026/27 (primary PDF on essex.gov.uk, set 12 Feb 2026; INHERITED by Reform UK which took the Executive 28 May 2026) + the AI DOGE directorate engine.

directorates.name: Education Excellence, Lifelong Learning and Employability
directorates._note: The GBP 835m DSG flows through here (gross GBP 919.6m).

cross_cutting._note: GBP 41m of new savings in 2026/27 (2.8% of net); engine risk-adjusts to ~GBP 22.77m EV. Directorate split is a net-budget-weighted allocation (flagged); no published per-directorate split.

mtfs_period: 2026/27 balanced; gap GBP 108m (27/28) rising to GBP 278m unfunded by 2029/30 (cumulative GBP 324m needed)

reserves._note: General Balance GBP 68.1m (flat across the MTFS); earmarked GBP 316.5m (Transformation 55.7m, Future Capital 52.1m, DSG General Risk 30.6m); restricted funds GBP 211.9m (Waste Reserve 112.1m the largest). GBP 1.8m one-off draw to balance 26/27.

risks.risk: MTFS gap of GBP 108m in 2027/28 rising to GBP 278m unfunded by 2029/30 (against a GBP 324m cumulative requirement), driven by demand (Social Care + Home to School Transport, GBP 225m by 2029/30) and inflation (GBP 156m). A Whole Council Transformation programme targets ~GBP 100m. Reform UK inherits this gap and the first Reform-set budget is 2027/28.
Adult Social Care and Health (GBP 670.7m net, the dominant spend) leads the savings; demand-led delivery risk. The GBP 41m 2026/27 savings were set by the outgoing administration and are inherited.

DSG / High Needs held via the DSG General Risk Reserve (GBP 30.6m, drawn down over the MTFS). The Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 nationally and was replaced by the High Needs Stability Grant; Essex-specific high-needs deficit position bears watching at the override end.

_inherited_budget_note: The 2026/27 budget was set by the OUTGOING Conservative administration on 12 Feb 2026. Reform UK won 7 May 2026 and took the Executive 28 May 2026, inheriting it. The first Reform-set budget will be 2027/28.
